notes.s: A door you build in your own head, and the shop behind it where the band talks you down.
notes.t: Fan song closing Love Yourself 轉 Tear in 2018. Magic Shop is a real psychodrama exercise: the therapist sets up an imaginary store where a client hands over something they fear and takes away something they need, and the group has also pointed to James Doty's memoir of the same name. The gratitude runs in both directions, which is unusual for a fan song, and Suga's verse is the part people quote alone, where he works out that wanting to be the best was never actually the want. The three-flower passage rewrites 하루만's morning glory as a way to finish well rather than a one-day deadline. You gave me the best of me became a standing fandom phrase and later an anniversary tagline.
k: Not a shop. It is a psychodrama technique, an imagined storefront where you trade a fear for something you need, so the chorus telling you to build a door in your own mind is that therapeutic exercise written out as an instruction.
필 땐 장미꽃처럼 / 흩날릴 땐 벚꽃처럼 / 질 땐 나팔꽃처럼

Three flowers assigned to three verbs: rose for blooming, cherry blossom for scattering, morning glory for closing. Korean has separate verbs for each stage of a flower's life, so the lines are doing something English has to paraphrase. The morning glory is the same flower 하루만 used as a deadline.

뭐랬어 is 뭐라고 했어 squeezed down, what did I say. Said after being proved right, it is close to what did I tell you. The 거랬잖아 in the next line is 거라고 했잖아 getting the same treatment. Reported speech collapsing like this is everywhere in casual Korean.

Literally river of stars, the Korean word for the Milky Way. The song keeps trading it against the English galaxy in the same breath, so your galaxy and 너의 은하수 are one image being passed back and forth between the two languages.
